extraction.name: RoboBench
extraction.description: RoboBench is a benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models as embodied brains for robotic manipulation. It evaluates five dimensions—Instruction Comprehension, Perception Reasoning, Generalized Planning, Affordance Prediction, and Failure Analysis—covering 14 capabilities, 25 tasks, and 6092 QA pairs using data from real robotic datasets and in-house collection.
extraction.creator: Yulin Luo; Chun-Kai Fan; Menghang Dong; Jiayu Shi; Mengdi Zhao; Bo-Wen Zhang; Cheng Chi; Jiaming Liu; Gaole Dai; Rongyu Zhang; Ruichuan An; Kun Wu; Zhengping Che; Shaoxuan Xie; Guocai Yao; Zhongxia Zhao; Pengwei Wang; Guang Liu; Zhongyuan Wang; Tiejun Huang; Shanghang Zhang
extraction.citeAs: Yulin Luo, Chun-Kai Fan, Menghang Dong, Jiayu Shi, Mengdi Zhao, Bo-Wen Zhang, Cheng Chi, Jiaming Liu, Gaole Dai, Rongyu Zhang, Ruichuan An, Kun Wu, Zhengping Che, Shaoxuan Xie, Guocai Yao, Zhongxia Zhao, Pengwei Wang, Guang Liu, Zhongyuan Wang, Tiejun Huang, and Shanghang Zhang. RoboBench: A Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark for Multimodal Large Language Models as Embodied Brain. arXiv:2510.17801v1, 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was built from open-source and in-house robotic data, combining large-scale real-world robotic datasets with curated in-house collection. For planning, the authors built a planning pool from high-quality robotic videos and extracted frame sequences as standardized inputs. Perception data were constructed from real robot data with metadata, curated attributes, segmented video steps, manual annotations, and human-labeled bounding boxes. Failure analysis data were collected from RoboMIND for execution-level failures, while planning-level failures were synthesized by perturbing correct instructions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis; Manual Human Curator; Software Collection; Others
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: planning-level failures are synthesized by perturbing correct instructions due to lack of real-world planning failure data
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: open-source and in-house robotic data; large-scale real-world robotic datasets; high-quality robotic videos from Open X-Embodiment, Lin et al. (2024a), Liu et al. (2024b;c), RH20T, RoboMIND, Mu et al. (2023), and Yang et al. (2024); real robot data with type and view metadata; curated static attributes; Gemini-segmented video steps; and RoboMIND execution-level failure data
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: RoboBench is built from open-source and in-house robotic data enriched with MLLM- and human-provided annotations; for planning, Gemini generates structured annotations (task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, and metadata) which are refined by human annotators; scene-centric perception uses manual annotations of relative positions and keypoint changes, task-centric perception uses human-labeled bounding boxes, affordance prediction samples representative frames annotated with static, dynamic, and mobile affordances, and execution-level failures are labeled by experts.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: After data construction, 20 professionally trained annotators conducted quality inspections validating linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness; a majority-vote strategy was used where items all models solved correctly were removed, and items all models failed underwent manual review and correction.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Existing planning failure data are lacking, so planning-level failures are synthesized by perturbing correct instructions; current models exhibit severe degradation on implicit instructions, weak robot-view recognition and temporal grounding, shallow affordance prediction, and poor execution-level failure diagnosis; planning remains the primary bottleneck, with struggles in dual-arm coordination, rare-object reasoning, and limited gains from multi-view inputs that still do not close the gap to human performance
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: RoboBench provides a comprehensive scaffold to quantify high-level cognition, clarify the role of the embodied brain, and guide the development of next-generation MLLMs toward more robust robotic intelligence.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: evaluate multimodal large language models as embodied brains for robotic manipulation; quantify high-level cognition across instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis; establish a leaderboard and offer actionable insights for advancing the embodied brain in robotic AI
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Implicit instructions are obtained by rewriting explicit instructions into demand-based requests using LLMs; planning-level failures are synthesized by perturbing correct instructions (wrong object, missing step, wrong order); and items that all models solve correctly are removed, whereas items all models fail to solve undergo manual review and correction.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data are standardized into multiple-choice QA; frame sequences are extracted as standardized inputs; representative frames are sampled for affordance annotation; general and task-specific filters are applied during construction, including image-quality and task-validity filtering and excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks.
